Product proposal / not a deployed product surface

What runs today.
What we plan to build.

The browser machine is the foundation. The ProofMesh proposal adds encrypted personal volumes, verified block delivery, and a market for reproducible software work. Each proposed surface has its own contract and acceptance gate.

Read the product specification →

Current machine

Browser Linux

A Rust RV64 virtual machine compiled to WebAssembly, with an unmodified Linux guest, console, and explicit storage, network, and display boundaries.

Open the demo ↗ · Boot guide →

Embedding boundary

The generated WasmMachine and WasmLinux assets plus the asynchronous Linux loader. Output and input use bytes; lifecycle and errors come from the controller.

Read the shipped boundary →

Proposed surfaces

Private volumes

Passkey and recovery slots unwrap volume keys for authenticated encrypted generations. This is proposed work; the current IndexedDB overlay is a separate boundary.

Verified delivery

HTTP, cache, WebRTC, and torrent-like sources deliver content-addressed blocks. Verification happens before a block enters the cache.

Work market

A frozen optimization ticket names the source, verifier, measurements, deadline, and reward. Builders submit artifacts and proof bundles.

Critic network

Independent critics check semantics, performance, security, dependencies, and reproducibility before a signed quorum settles a ticket.

The next proof

The first product milestone is a local builder/critic loop against a real wasm-vm workload. Distributed delivery follows a proven storage boundary; process placement across browser nodes comes later.
